cards.front: Recall a key point about Knitting Weaving and Crochet
cards.back: Knitting and crochet create fabric from yarn through interlocking loops — knit/purl for knitting; chain, double crochet, treble for crochet.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Knitting Weaving and Crochet
cards.back: Tension/gauge determines fabric density — always make a tension square before starting a project to ensure correct sizing.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Knitting Weaving and Crochet
cards.back: Weaving interlaces warp (lengthwise) and weft (crosswise) threads — tabby (plain) weave and twill weave are fundamental structures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Knitting Weaving and Crochet
cards.back: Colour work techniques (Fair Isle, intarsia) create patterns within knitted fabric through colour changes.

cards.front: What should you know about textile design exam tips?
cards.back: Show PROCESS — include samples at different stages. Annotate with TECHNIQUE NAMES and vocabulary. Demonstrate TENSION control. Compare the visual/textural qualities of different techniques.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Knitting and crochet are the same thing — just different names for looping yarn. Correct: Knitting uses TWO needles to create fabric from multiple live stitches; crochet uses ONE hook to complete each stitch before moving on. cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Knitting Weaving and Crochet
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Knitting Weaving and Crochet using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.
